title: Target
description: A managed guest: its Proxmox settings and its Blocks.

name.description: Unique per kind. Lower case letters, digits, '-' and '.'.

disk.description: GiB. Grow only (D-291, D-299): a proposal that lowers the value of an existing Target is refused, and a Plan never shrinks a disk (Proxmox cannot). A grow is disruptive (it cannot be undone), passes the disk gate (D-219), and needs a running guest; a VM also needs an agent that runs the grow command. vm: the boot disk scsi0; lxc: the root file system rootfs, at least 2.

power.description: Desired power state (D-291, D-299). Missing: Plumb does not manage it (as before slice 4: a create starts the guest, a stop outside Plumb is no drift). running: a stopped guest is drift; a start is reversible. stopped: a stop is disruptive and needs allow_restart; agent resources of a stopped Target are skipped, its offline agent is no Issue, and a disk grow is refused. A new Target is created, enrolled and applied first, then stopped.

tags.description: Proxmox tags, the exact set (D-291, D-299). Missing: Plumb does not manage tags; []: no tags. Order does not matter. A change is reversible. Lower case only, so the set compares exactly; a tag that a person adds in Proxmox is drift.

ip.description: dhcp or an IPv4 address in CIDR form. Create-only. Known limit (D-192, D-220, D-223), not a validation rule: a stock Ubuntu 26.04 image used directly by a Target can sometimes stay on DHCP until its first restart; use dhcp or an Image built by Plumb.

gateway.description: IPv4 gateway for a static ip. Create-only.

user.description: Bootstrap user that cloud-init creates. Create-only. vm only: an LXC Target has no bootstrap user (refused; use a Block such as deploy-user, D-226).

ssh_keys.description: Public keys of the bootstrap user, without options. Create-only. lxc: the keys go to root (D-226).

nics.description: More network cards after the first one (bridge, ip and gateway above), at most 3. Plumb chooses their MAC addresses. Each bridge, and each bridge with a VLAN tag, must be named when Plumb is installed. Adding, removing or moving a card is disruptive. Not for an adopted Target. At most one gateway in total. Planned: refused until slice 7 serves it (T-219).

tag.description: VLAN tag. The bridge must be VLAN-aware; the install must name bridge:tag (--extra-vlan).

ip.description: dhcp or an IPv4 address in CIDR form. Missing: the NIC is up without an address.

gateway.description: IPv4 gateway for a static ip. At most one gateway over all NICs.

allow_restart.description: Plumb may restart or stop this guest (D-194, D-291). false: no Run stops or restarts the guest while it runs; a change of cores or memory of a VM waits until you stop and start it, a re-enrollment of a running VM is refused, and power: stopped is refused. true: a Run may restart a VM (clean shutdown, hard power-off after 2 minutes, then start) and may stop a VM or an LXC for power: stopped; the Plan shows it before the approval. It is a rule of Plumb, not a Proxmox setting: never drift, no override. cores and memory change live on a container.

backup.description: Backups of the guest by Plumb, to the one backup storage named at install. A backup does not change the guest. Missing: no backups by Plumb. Planned: refused until slice 7 serves it (T-221).

keep.description: How many scheduled backups Plumb keeps; the oldest above it go. Beside them Plumb keeps at most 2 backups made by 'Back up now'. Lowering keep deletes backups: that Plan is destructive and says how many go. Removing the backup field stops the backups and deletes none.

id.description: Id of this use of the Block. Default: the Block name. Two uses of the same Block need different ids. It names the order group of the rendered resources.

blocks.description: Blocks of the target. The same Block can be used more than once, with different ids and parameters.

adopted.description: The Target holds a guest that a person made and put into the pool (D-373, D-386). It has no image. node and vmid are create-only: they name the bound guest; another guest needs a new adoption. Its create-only settings and container features are not compared (D-391). Delete of the Target only unbinds the guest unless delete_guest is true (D-388).

delete_guest.description: true: deleting this Target deletes the Proxmox guest and its disks. Setting it is human-only and destructive (adopted-guest-delete, D-388).

overrides.description: Resource id → attributes that replace the rendered ones. Written by Accept and by raw mode.
